item.title: Chinese executive convicted in case linked to Bangkok tower collapse
item.description: A court in Thailand on Wednesday found a Chinese executive and Thai shareholders of a Thai subsidiary of a Chinese state-owned construction company guilty of illegally operating a business in Thailand in a case related to the collapse of a Bangkok office building last year. At least 92 people died on March 28, 2025, when an earthquake struck the partially built high-rise, which was to house the State Audit Office. item.title: Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first black US House speaker
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader on Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 cast against his nomination, according to US media. item.title: Japan’s Takaichi meets Putin in rare talks amid strained ties with Russia
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi met Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday, marking a rare high-level contact at a time of deeply strained relations over Moscow’s war in Ukraine and the recent arrest of a Japanese journalist on espionage allegations. The talks, held on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leaders’ summit in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, lasted about 30 minutes. item.title: Islam projected to surpass Christianity as world’s largest religion by 2035
item.description: Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world’s largest religion by 2035, according to detailed projections released on Wednesday by the Pew Research Centre. Pew, which has been issuing authoritative reports on religious demography for 25 years, said both Islam and Christianity were growing, but Islam was growing much faster. A key reason, Pew said, was that Muslims tended to have more children than other major religious groups. “It’s the babies,” said Pew senior demographer Conrad...

item.title: Rare hug and roaring flyover set stage for historic firsts at Apec in Shenzhen
item.description: It was a day of firsts in Shenzhen on Wednesday when Chinese President Xi Jinping personally greeted his American counterpart Donald Trump at the city airport, setting up a historic start to the Apec summit. It was the first time in nearly seven decades that China’s top leader had welcomed a visiting foreign head of state at an airport, and it set the stage for an international event that is likely to lead to a joint declaration by the 21 Apec members on Thursday.
